headline: Highest risk is data leakage from Chatwoot’s customer data into EMQX’s broad network egress; other pairwise risks are mostly low or medium due to limited documented overlap.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A direct prompt-injection bridge is not documented, but Chatwoot can ingest customer messages and EMQX exposes an HTTP API, so a manual or workflow bridge could pass attacker-controlled content between them. No shared filesystem or parser is shown, so the pathway is limited and not default-dangerous.
conditions: IF Chatwoot message content is copied into EMQX-managed workflows or HTTP payloads without sanitization, injection risk exists.
IF EMQX routes inbound content into downstream automation that Chatwoot later reads as instructions, the bridge becomes exploitable.
mitigations: Sanitize and strip instruction-like text from copied messages.
Use a fixed schema for any Chatwoot-to-EMQX payloads.
Require human review before forwarding customer text.
Log and reject payloads containing control tokens or markup.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to distinguish user content from system instructions.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, and messages, while EMQX has broad network egress. Even without a shared workspace, any integration that forwards Chatwoot content to EMQX can leak sensitive customer data to external endpoints. The profiles do not show a default shared storage path, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF Chatwoot conversation records are forwarded into EMQX topics or HTTP requests, customer data leaves Chatwoot’s boundary.
IF EMQX subscribers or downstream services are external, the forwarded data can be exposed beyond the original support workflow.
mitigations: Minimize fields sent from Chatwoot to EMQX.
Mask emails, phone numbers, and order IDs before forwarding.
Restrict EMQX topics to non-sensitive test data.
Review outbound destinations on both systems.
requires-engineering: enforce field-level allowlists on integration payloads.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress, but neither profile shows filesystem write, git mutation, or shared mutable resources. That makes direct capability conflict unlikely. The only overlap is network/API use, which is not enough for a higher severity under the rubric.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same external API or queue, write conflicts can occur.
IF an orchestrator maps both agents onto one mutable resource without locking, race conditions become possible.
mitigations: Assign separate API credentials per agent.
Avoid shared mutable queues or topics.
Serialize writes through one coordinator.
Monitor for duplicate or conflicting updates.
requires-engineering: add locking or optimistic concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Chatwoot produces customer-facing support content and EMQX can consume and relay it via HTTP API. If EMQX treats Chatwoot output as authoritative, errors or hallucinated details can cascade into downstream automation or routing. The profiles do not prove verification steps, so the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF EMQX ingests Chatwoot-generated text without validation, incorrect support content can propagate.
IF downstream automation acts on that content, the cascade can affect multiple work products or actions.
mitigations: Insert a validation step before EMQX consumes Chatwoot output.
Require structured fields instead of free text.
Flag low-confidence Chatwoot outputs for review.
Limit downstream actions to read-only previews.
requires-engineering: add provenance and confidence metadata end-to-end.

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot clearly touches customer data and related support records, while EMQX is documented here only as touching IoT data. The profiles do not show a residency, certification, or retention mismatch, so compliance risk is present only if regulated customer data is routed into EMQX. One-sided citation is sufficient because the issue is Chatwoot-origin data flowing outward.
conditions: IF regulated customer records from Chatwoot are forwarded into EMQX storage or logs, compliance obligations may expand.
IF EMQX retention exceeds Chatwoot retention for the same records, deletion and export handling can diverge.
mitigations: Do not forward regulated fields into EMQX.
Set short retention on any mirrored records.
Document the data flow and lawful basis.
Review vendor terms for both systems.
requires-engineering: align deletion/export workflows across systems.
